item.title: Credit-Builder Cards UK: Best Cards to Build Credit in 2026
item.description:
Quick answer: Credit-builder cards are designed for people with poor or no credit history. They have low limits (£150–£1,500) and high APRs (30–40%), but if you spend a small amount monthly and pay in full every month, you pay zero interest while building your credit score. After 6–12 months of good behaviour, you can graduate to standard cards. Best providers: Aqua, Capital One, Vanquis, and Barclaycard Forward.

item.title: Overdrafts Explained UK: Costs, Rules, and How to Get Out
item.description: Quick answer: A UK bank overdraft lets you spend more than is in your account, up to an agreed limit. Since FCA rule changes in 2020, overdrafts are charged as a single annual interest rate (typically 35-40% APR) — daily and monthly fees were abolished. Overdrafts are one of the most expensive forms of borrowing. To clear yours: switch to a 0% overdraft account, use a 0% balance transfer card, or pay it down £50/month. Source: FCA — Overdrafts.

item.title: UK Savings Account Rates Comparison 2026: Best Accounts Compared
item.description:
Quick answer: UK savings rates in 2026 range from roughly 4.5–5.5% on the best easy-access accounts and 4.8–5.2% on fixed-rate bonds (1-year). The best regular savers pay 5–7% but cap monthly deposits. Cash ISA rates are similar to non-ISA equivalents but all returns are tax-free within your £20,000 annual ISA allowance. Always check current rates on comparison sites — they change weekly.
